criteria.description: Stable-thread catalogs retain replay mappings, journals and receipts, read/source records, change/review dependencies, and commentary across workspaces, routing remaps, forks, and restarts; inherited visible dependencies gain ownership and shared records survive removal of one owner.

Maintenance expires sessions after 14 inactive days, runs age sweeps at most hourly during preparation, and reclaims least-recently-active inactive sessions under pressure before publishing new durable facts.
Capacity decisions include catalogs, indexes, and pending replacements while preserving the 1 GiB managed-data, 256 MiB retained-read, 16 MiB commentary, and 32 MiB per-record boundaries.

Cross-process leases and atomic publication protect active turns, preparation, handoffs, workers, yielded work, and snapshot adoption; terminals release only matching idle leases, stale terminals preserve newer work, and shutdown releases process-owned leases.

Cleanup removes only exact Mekugi-managed records, never follows symlinks or removes unknown or user-owned data, preserves leased and shared dependencies, does not alter live process authority, and reports failures without claiming success.

Legacy ownership is adopted only from reliable visible replay, journal, read, or change evidence; recent unattributed records stay protected, old unattributed records use modification age, and missing references explain expiry or storage pressure without rerunning operations.

Change retirement preserves stream high-water counters, exposes partial retirement, retains dependencies reached through change reads, source records, and duplicate cursors, and pins complete dependency chains for active readers.

Protected-capacity failures identify required bytes, the limiting budget, and a recovery action; read and journal publication retain underlying causes; successful cleanup and auxiliary failures use the existing non-invasive user or worker reporting paths.

Lifetime ceilings on thread, source, usage, journal-thread, and mutation-receipt identities are removed while live queues, per-child queues, journal items, response publication, and record sizes remain bounded; queue recovery and token-overflow behavior remain correct.

Provider responses, tool results, command execution, replay payloads, routing, and continuation semantics remain compatible; owning user, architecture, router, journal, commentary, and read documentation and focused regression tests are complete, with no new dependencies or unrelated changes.

preparation: bun install --cwd plugins --frozen-lockfile && bun build plugins/tools.ts --outfile ./internal/router/toolplugin/dist/tools.js --production --target node --format esm --external hpatch:core/v1 --external mekugi:core/v1 && go mod download
evaluator_guidance: Use isolated temporary replay roots and deterministic clocks or timestamps. Exercise public or existing package-level behavior rather than requiring the reference solution's internal types or helper names. Cover the stated concurrency and storage boundaries without reading the excluded solution.
